question: In a 68-year-old patient with new onset headache, pain and prolonged morning stiffness in scapular and pelvic girdles of several weeks of evolution that presents unilateral bruising of sudden onset, what treatment among the following would establish before confirming the diagnosis?

options.opb: Methylprednisolone 1 g i.v. daily for three days.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "New onset headache" -> "Pain and prolonged morning stiffness" -> "Scapular and pelvic girdle involvement" -> "Possible polymyalgia rheumatica" -> "Prednisone 10 mg daily v.o." -> 85%
CHAIN: "Unilateral bruising of sudden onset" -> "Possible giant cell arteritis" -> "High suspicion of temporal arteritis" -> "Prednisone 10 mg daily v.o." -> 80%
CHAIN: "68-year-old patient" -> "New onset headache" -> "Prolonged morning stiffness" -> "Consider inflammatory condition" -> "Prednisone 10 mg daily v.o." -> 75%
CHAIN: "Sudden onset unilateral bruising" -> "Possible vascular involvement" -> "Consider temporal arteritis" -> "Prednisone 10 mg daily v.o." -> 70%
CHAIN: "Headache and stiffness" -> "Age 68" -> "Consider polymyalgia rheumatica" -> "Prednisone 10 mg daily v.o." -> 80%
analysis: The clinical presentation suggests possible giant cell arteritis (GCA), especially given the age, new onset headache, and symptoms consistent with polymyalgia rheumatica (PMR). The sudden onset of unilateral bruising could indicate temporal artery involvement. In such cases, immediate treatment with corticosteroids is recommended to prevent complications like vision loss. Prednisone is typically used in this scenario to quickly reduce inflammation while awaiting confirmatory diagnosis.
